title: SR-1.25 A cloud seat allowed to assign tasks addresses one local seat, never all
request: Closes G90: with bus.cloud_tasks on, a cloud seat's task to all is accepted (src/engine/bus.mjs:307 checks the type, not the address), while docs/BUS.md:100-101 grants a task to a local seat and nothing else. Found by the memev twin on 30 October 2026 at main be457db (a sealed run in the twin's evidence). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: QL-1.02, SR-1.28. Sensitive path (the oplog): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge.

tasks.title: Address checked with the type
requirements: a cloud seat's task is accepted only when it is addressed to one named local seat; all, a cloud seat and an unknown seat are refused with the reason
the address is checked before anything is written: a refused cloud send leaves the bus log, its size and every seat's unread unchanged, writes no seat file and queues no commit

a seat is a cloud seat when its device's current kind in the registry is cloud-connector, whatever its name, number suffix, sub-seat or rename; a seat on an enrolled remote computer (the owner's own device) is a local seat; a removed seat, a seat whose computer was revoked and a seat whose device is not in the registry are refused

a cloud seat's task 'to' must be a string naming one registered local seat exactly, compared with the seat names the bus holds and never through the file-name mapping; an array, any other type (0, false and the empty string included; only a missing 'to' means the lead), 'all' in any case or with padding, and a name with a control character are refused

with cloud_tasks on, the refusal for 'all' or a cloud seat says a cloud task goes to one local seat and does not mention turning cloud_tasks on; an unknown seat is refused with code not_found and 'no seat <name>'
a caller that is not local and has no device record is refused every bus call with code forbidden and a message naming the missing device record; it is never mapped onto this host's seats

a cloud seat is never the lead (SR-1.28 refuses one); a cloud seat's task to the operator alias is a task to the trusted lead: with cloud_tasks off it is refused like every cloud task, with cloud_tasks on it is stored addressed to the lead's name at send time, and with no lead set it is refused

memev doctor flags cloud tasks to 'all' or to a cloud seat that are already in the bus logs from before this change, with the daemon running as well as stopped; a line counts as a cloud task when the device whose log holds it is a cloud-connector in the registry, whatever its from name
docs/BUS.md says a cloud task goes to one named local seat, that a seat on an enrolled remote computer counts as local, and that 'all', a cloud seat and an unknown seat are refused
with cloud_tasks off every cloud task is refused, whatever its address, with a message naming cloud_tasks; other types from a cloud seat go to the operator alias only, as before
a sender whose device's current kind is not cloud-connector (this host, or an enrolled remote computer) is never held to the cloud rules, whatever the request's local flag says

the lead that the operator alias resolves to passes the same local-seat test at send time as a seat named directly: a lead whose device is now a cloud-connector, a removed lead, a lead whose computer was revoked or is not in the registry, and a bus/operator.json naming any of these make a cloud task to the alias refused; a line written by a seat whose device is a cloud-connector never carries operator: true

a seat whose device's current kind is cloud-connector is a cloud seat even when the request is local or its client is the terminal (cli): it never posts as the operator alias or as this host's terminal
the cloud_tasks setting turns cloud tasks on only when its value is the boolean true; any other value, a string such as 'false', 'off' or '0' included, counts as off
a cloud seat writes no join hello and no automatic comms-check acknowledgement: every line in a cloud device's log is one its seat sent, so nothing from a cloud seat is addressed to 'all'
an accepted cloud task is delivered only to the seat it names: a seat record's renamed_from never makes another seat, a cloud seat included, receive it

a device's kind is the one it was enrolled with: a kind inferred from the User-Agent or any other request header never lifts the proof requirement and never turns a remote computer into a cloud connector, and a record an earlier version switched that way reads as a remote computer again (issue 266; the stopgap on main already does this, and this contract keeps it)
